title: Given an array of numbers, find all unique triplets that add up to zero. Each triplet must be unique, and the solution should avoid duplicates. (LeetCode: 3Sum)
shortTitle: Triplet Sum to Zero (3Sum with Two Pointers)
keyPoints: Sort the array, fix one element, then use two pointers on the remaining portion to find pairs that complete the triplet
Skip duplicates at two levels: skip repeated fixed elements and skip repeated pair values after recording a triplet
Sorting enables both the two-pointer squeeze and straightforward duplicate avoidance
Early exit when the fixed element is positive, since no triplet starting there can sum to zero
Time is O(n^2) from the fixed element loop times the linear two-pointer sweep
The same skeleton generalizes to k-Sum by recursively fixing elements and dropping to a two-pointer base case

s1_definition.oneliner: Sort, fix one, then two-pointer the rest; skip duplicates at every level.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **3Sum (Triplet Sum to Zero)** – find all unique sets of three elements whose sum is zero.
- **Sort first** – sorting the array in O(n log n) enables the two-pointer squeeze and duplicate skipping.
- **Fix and sweep** – for each fixed element, use a left and right pointer to find pairs summing to its negation.
- **Duplicate avoidance** – skip repeated fixed elements at the outer level and skip repeated pair values at the inner level.
- **Complexity** – O(n^2) time from the outer loop times the linear sweep; sorting is dominated by the quadratic work.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine Rajesh at the National Bank of India has a list of signed adjustments on an account: credits (positive) and debits (negative). He needs to find every unique group of three adjustments that perfectly cancel out to zero rupees. He sorts the adjustments, fixes one at a time, and for each fixed one asks Priya to find two others from the remaining list that together cancel it, using the two-pointer squeeze from both ends.

sections.s6_takeaway:
The 3Sum problem asks for every unique group of three numbers that adds up to zero. The efficient solution sorts the array first, then iterates through it fixing each element as the first member of the triplet. For each fixed element, a two-pointer sweep over the remaining portion finds pairs that complete the sum to zero.

Duplicate avoidance is clean because sorting places identical values adjacent. At the outer level you skip a fixed element that equals the previous one. After recording a triplet at the inner level, you advance both pointers past any repeated values. This guarantees no duplicate triplets without needing a hash set.

In the reconciliation service at the National Bank of India, an account accumulates signed adjustments through the day: credits positive, debits negative. The audit team needs every unique group of three adjustments that exactly cancel to zero, because such trios signal a reversal pattern worth reviewing. The sorted two-pointer approach produces a clean, duplicate-free list efficiently.

The senior-level insight is that the same sort-fix-squeeze skeleton extends directly to k-Sum by recursively fixing elements and dropping to a two-pointer base case. Recognizing that 3Sum is just one instance of this general pattern lets you adapt quickly in an interview.

Remember one sentence: sort, fix one element, two-pointer the rest for the complementary pair, and skip duplicates at every level.
